oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: node/gpu-node-42 reported repeated `CUDA OOM` errors while headroom reported as available (metric: gpu.mem.headroom>2GB). Auto-page to oncall.
Emma L: I'm on it. seeing spiking OOMs across a handful of replicas for model `rdw-13b-v2` on node-42. headroom metric looks normal, allocator logs show repeated `reserve_block` failures.
Raj P: from a glance that sounds like prefetch + kv-cache reservation getting torn down/fragmented. can you paste the allocator logs?
Emma L: pasted sample below from node-42 (truncated):
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] allocator: reserve_block 0x7f9a... size=248MB -> success
[2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] kvcache: prefetch request id=5634 seq=12 prefetched=192MB
[2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] allocator: fallback allocate size=72MB -> failed: no contiguous block
[2026-03-15T14:02:14Z] runtime: cuda_api: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (error 2)
[2026-03-15T14:02:14Z] runtime: triggering spill -> pageout to host
```
Emma L: headroom telemetry shows ~2.3GB free but fragmentation heatmap shows lots of small free chunks.
Dana M: node-level fragmentation can give a false sense of headroom. if reserved blocks are pinned and KV cache holds lots of small allocations we hit OOM for contiguous allocations.
SRE-Lead: agree. quick mitigation options: 1) disable prefetch on the affected deploys, 2) reduce kv-cache reservable size, 3) force graceful recycle of affected pods to compact memory, 4) route traffic to Dedicated pool as a fallback. Which do we want as immediate?
Raj P: immediate: disable prefetch and lower kv-cache from 320MB -> 128MB on canaries, then drain node-42 and let pods reschedule. that should avoid large contiguous allocations failing.
Emma L: doing canary flag flip now for `rdw-13b-v2` in region-us-west: ``kubectl -n inference set env deploy/rdw-13b-v2 PREFETCH_ENABLED=false --record``
Emma L: also changing kv cache config via runtime feature flag: ``curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/flags -d '{"service":"rdw-13b-v2","kv_cache_limit_mb":128}''`` (cc: @Raj P)
Raj P: I'll start a rolling drain of node-42 to force compaction: ``kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data``. prepping to shift traffic to dedicated-pool-1 if we see >1% error rates.
Support-Bot: Noted. Creating incident ticket INC-20260315-42 and notifying customer success for impacted accounts with potential 502s.
Emma L: after disabling prefetch, I still see two OOM traces but error rate fell from 8% -> 1.2% in the last 3 minutes. good sign.
SRE-Lead: keep an eye on paging rates. if we see sustained host-pageouts we'll need to increase slab coalescing thresholds in the allocator (longer-term fix).
Emma L: captured host diagnostics: ``nvidia-smi topo --matrix`` shows expected layout. `pmap`-style dump of GPU allocations demonstrates many 8–16MB free holes.
Raj P: that implies contiguity problem. For immediate mitigation we should also bump kernel reservation heuristic to allow a larger contiguous reserve on new allocations. I can push a hotfix to the runtime: patch allocator to prefer coalescing on free. However that's risky to rollout mid-incident.
Dana M: alternative: compact by executing controlled graceful restarts for the largest consumers only (route traffic away first). which pods have highest kv-cache consumption?
Emma L: list of top pods (cpu/gpu mem):
- rdw-13b-v2-7f9a (node-42) kv-cache 312MB
- rdw-13b-v2-5a2c (node-42) kv-cache 304MB
- rdw-13b-v2-9cde (node-42) kv-cache 296MB
Emma L: I'm evicting the two largest now, leaving a single canary running with prefetch off.
SRE-Lead: timeline and customer impact note for postmortem: root alert at 14:02Z, degraded from 14:02–14:11Z, partial recovery by 14:06Z after prefetch off, node drain complete 14:11Z. record per-customer error percentages: acct-omega 5.7% errors, acct-alpha 0.9%.
Support-Bot: Sent automated customer messages to users with >1% errors: acct-omega notified, CS assigned to follow up.
Raj P: after draining node and restarting pods, fragmentation heatmap shows larger contiguous blocks available. tail of allocator logs:```
[2026-03-15T14:09:20Z] allocator: coalesce freed blocks -> new contiguous 512MB
[2026-03-15T14:09:21Z] runtime: allocate size=480MB -> success
```
Emma L: confirmed model traffic back to normal for most routes. Error rate trending to baseline (<0.2%).
Dana M: followups we need to track: - add a runtime metric that reports contiguous-free-block-size distribution (not just total headroom) - limit default prefetch for large models unless explicit opt-in - add an allocator flag for aggressive coalescing during low-load windows - trial a background compaction job to periodically defragment GPU heap
SRE-Lead: assign owners: Emma (postmortem), Raj (allocator telemetry + hotfix PR), Dana (runtime defaults + compaction job), SRE-Lead (customer impact summary & SLA check).
Emma L: I'll open a postmortem draft and attach logs/heap-dumps. starting with title: "Prefetch-induced fragmentation -> CUDA OOM despite reported headroom".
Raj P: creating a low-risk runtime PR to expose contiguous-block metric to console. link to PR will be in the postmortem.
Support-Bot: Incident INC-20260315-42 updated: severity=sev2, impacted-customers=[acct-omega], slack-thread=https://redwood.slack/2958000000.
SRE-Lead: final note for oncall handoff: if similar alerts spike, immediately flip PREFETCH_ENABLED=false for the model family and route canary traffic to dedicated-pool-1, escalate to eng-ml if error rate >3% after mitigations. handing off to next oncall @Dana M.
Dana M: taking handoff. I'll coordinate postmortem + customer notes. thx all :thumbsup:
